item.title: Socrates Restaurant (1965-2010) Returns to Greenpoint for One Day Only
item.dc:creator: Julia M
item.description:
Longtime Greenpointers might remember Socrates Restaurant, an unassuming neighborhood diner at 651 Manhattan Avenue that quietly served the community for decades.

The post Socrates Restaurant (1965-2010) Returns to Greenpoint for One Day Only appeared first on Greenpointers.
item.content:encoded:
Longtime Greenpointers might remember Socrates Restaurant, an unassuming neighborhood diner at 651 Manhattan Avenue that quietly served the community for decades.

After immigrating from Cyprus, Charlie and Doula opened Socrates on October 13, 1965, and ran the restaurant with Charlie’s younger brother Mike until retiring and selling it in 2001. Charlie worked the front of the house, greeting regulars and pouring coffee, while Mike served as head chef and Doula was the baker.

item.title: Top Chef Alum’s Mythily Opens in Williamsburg
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Rosini-Gentile
item.description:
Named after her grandmother.

The post Top Chef Alum’s Mythily Opens in Williamsburg appeared first on Greenpointers.
item.content:encoded:
Mythily, a new Indian restaurant from Top Chef alum Rasika Venkatesa, opens today in Williamsburg at 129 Havemeyer Street.

Mythily is named after Chef Venkatesa’s grandmother, who was her earliest inspiration. Chef Venkatesa was born and raised in India and said her grandmother’s cooking showed her how food could bring family together and honor their culture.

item.title: Italian Sandwich Shop Malavita Starts Dinner Service This Weekend
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Rosini-Gentile
item.description:
Adding dinner was always the plan.

The post Italian Sandwich Shop Malavita Starts Dinner Service This Weekend appeared first on Greenpointers.
item.content:encoded:
Malavita (614 Manhattan Ave.), an Italian sandwich shop that opened in April, is adding dinner service starting this Friday, September 25.

By day, Malavita will continue to be a sandwich shop, and at night, it will transform into an osteria, which is an Italian word for a casual restaurant, similar to a bistro.

Malavita’s owner, Greenpoint local Keith Pulitano, told Greenpointers that “adding a dinner menu alongside the all day sandwiches was always the plan.”
